answer: Histories are stored in velvet, checked in timber, and sable shows each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 5 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases since the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 1852 identities would post 4059 proofs and burn roughly 9 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
